courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

lectures.title: How To Connect to a Backend

cues.en: Of course we first of all need to understand how an Ionic app connects to a back-end, so to a server
running in the web where we want to store data.
Now you could think that we use a database, SQL or NoSQL, doesn't matter and we simply connect
our Ionic app to that to store data there
but this is not what we do because directly accessing the database would be a really insecure.
For example, we would have to store the credentials for accessing the database in our Ionic app code
and since this in the end is all Javascript, people could get access to it and therefore, we definitely
don't want to directly connect to a database,
instead we connect to an API exposed on a server.
This could be a REST API, could be a GraphQL API,
could be web sockets.
It is an API that accepts HTTP requests, that then handles them, that run some code which is defined
on the server which we don't care about
if we haven't written that code at least and which we can communicate with.
So the server in the end or the logic written there interacts with the database that also runs
on the server, that also runs in the cloud
so to say and we just interact with that API to send requests and receive responses. These requests and
responses will be exchanged in the JSON format,
so we're not sending HTML around or anything like that,
instead we'll send JSON data because that is easy to read in code and easy to work with, especially
when building an app with Javascript as we're doing it here.
Now that server, this API, could of course be written by you, it could be your own custom back-end
or you use a managed service like Firebase or AWS Mobile Hub or anything like that.
In this course, we'll use Firebase and whilst Firebase sounds like it is just a database, Firebase is really
a managed service that gives you an API to communicate with,
that gives you a database to which this API will then communicate and way more and we'll use a
couple of these features so that we don't have to worry about writing back-end code in this course because
this isn't really the focus of the course, we want to focus on the front-end,
we want to focus on Ionic.
